set.title: [af] The milestone ladder: M1-M7 and the alpha
set.body:
## Destination

The Linux prototype becomes the alpha of DIRECTION.md: several sensors, agent identity, tamper sensing with quarantine, a deterministic engine, local traces, opt-in telemetry design — released only after every step passed its exit gate, with the research backend explicitly out.

## Notes

- Spec and source of truth: `docs/MILESTONES.md` (the ladder, deliverables, exit gates). Direction and principles: `docs/DIRECTION.md`; bindings: `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- Ladder order: M1 → M2 → {M4, M5} → M6. M3 and ML run in parallel with M1/M2 (no shared code). M7 never blocks.
- A milestone is done when its exit-gate measurement is committed next to runnable code — not when the code compiles.
- The benign corpus is the quiet test for every milestone that can ask a question. Quiet is the feature.
- The ledger blocked-count (74 scenarios today) is the progress metric: each sensor that lands unblocks a counted set.
- A failed gate is a result: recorded in the ticket, absorbed by the plan.

## Out of scope (for this whole plan)

macOS; attach-mode observation; the enterprise tier (privileged service, central policy, Group Policy); network content inspection; io_uring coverage; the research backend and analysis-agent automation; any Windows code.

set.title: [af-1] M1 — The bypass harness
set.body:
## Goal

One matrix, two sensors. The shipping firewall is exec `ptrace` plus the `seccomp` filter. Before any new sensor is argued for, measure what these two hold, see, and miss — with attacks on purpose, not by anecdote.

## Deliverables

- `research/bypass/`: a suite of small controlled programs, one per technique. Seed list, each grounded in a measurement or a catalogue scenario: a static binary; raw `syscall()` file and network access from a running program; `setsid` and double-fork; a process that outlives the session; `io_uring` batch I/O; delete and rename (no event kind exists); dangerous content passed by file name instead of argv; a credential-file read under both filter modes; an attempt to find and kill the monitor.
- A benign corpus: a scripted normal dev session — `cargo build`, `npm test`, `git`, `kubectl get` — that must never trigger anything.
- The matrix: technique x sensor mode (`write-only`, `all-opens`, `off`), each cell `held | seen | silent`, with the rule that fired or the reason none could. Every row cites the `evade` scenario it maps to, where one exists.

## Exit gate

The matrix is committed with runnable code and a `FINDINGS.md`; the benign corpus produces zero questions in the same run; every `silent` cell names the mechanism that would be needed to see it.

## Unlocks

The true rank of the external stack's gaps; the job description for the in-process sensor ([af-2]); the tamper techniques [af-5] must sense; the rows that decide whether correlation has anything to catch ([af-6]).

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M1.

set.title: [af-2] M2 — The in-process sensor (LD_PRELOAD shim)
set.body:
## Goal

The `LD_PRELOAD` shim of DIRECTION.md §3.1, measured as a sensor. It reports. It never decides.

## Deliverables

- `research/spikes/inprocess/`: a shim that emits `af-core` events — exec family, file access, network libc calls, `dlopen`, environment manipulation — with propagation into descendants where it can, and a registration record so the firewall knows exactly which sensor instances it installed. That registration is the B.5 fact that [af-5] and [af-6] key on.
- The [af-1] matrix re-run with the shim active: which cells move from `silent` to `seen`, and which move to `held` — the shim itself never holds; a hold can only come from correlation with an external sensor.
- Bench numbers for the shim, and the semantic gain in one number: what fraction of the benign corpus's interesting actions the sensor reports that argv-only cannot see (stdin context, about-to-exec).

## Exit gate

Schema-valid events in a trace; the matrix rows updated; overhead measured; and the DECISIONS test already applied — sensor silence, keyed to installed instances, fires zero times on the benign corpus. The gate decides: keep the sensor in the product, or demote it to research telemetry. Both are acceptable results.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M2.

set.title: [af-3] M3 — Agent identity: detection, propagation, escape
set.body:
## Goal

Answer question 1 of DIRECTION.md §11 with numbers: how reliably can we identify AI-agent root processes, and does the identity hold through the tree?

## Deliverables

- A detector interface in `af-core` (plugin shape, confidence score) and the first detectors: known executables and argv patterns, package-manager installation metadata, dependency manifests, characteristic environment variables.
- Identity as a fact of the provenance graph: the tagged root, propagated to every descendant; events carry the agent.
- Escape detection as the negative case: a descendant that detaches from the tree (`setsid`, double-fork) is flagged as *unlinked*, never as *foreign* (the B.6 liveness fact, shared with [af-5]).

## Exit gate

On a fixture corpus of agent and non-agent commands, precision and recall are measured and committed; a normal non-agent dev session receives zero agent tags; a fixture escape is flagged. Quiet applies to identity too: a false agent tag is worse than no tag, because everything downstream keys on it.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M3.

set.title: [af-4] ML — Quiet by construction (Landlock, L0)
set.body:
## Goal

Ship the one mechanism that removes questions instead of asking them. Measured at 1.0x, sound by construction, enforced in the kernel (DETECTION-RESEARCH §4).

## Deliverables

- Re-measure the current 144-rule pack: which `approval_required` and `deny` rules are "always no, everywhere" and can move into the kernel. The spike measured 10 of the earlier 69-rule pack; today's number is the gate's input.
- The L2 explainer: when the kernel refuses, the session names the rule the kernel enforced. DETECTION-RESEARCH is explicit that an unexplained `EACCES` is how the cheapest layer gets switched off.
- e2e: a credential read two shells deep fails with no prompt, and the session explains why.

## Exit gate

The count of questions removed, measured on the pack and on the benign corpus; the bench shows no measurable cost; zero new questions added. This milestone can only shrink the interruption budget.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §ML.

set.title: [af-5] M4 — Tamper sensing and the quarantine flow
set.body:
## Goal

Fail-closed becomes sensed. Today the tree dies with the monitor (`EXITKILL`) and a monitor-less call breaks (`ENOSYS`); nothing notices the attempt. DIRECTION.md §6 makes the attempt a high-severity signal, and the decision log binds how: keyed to the firewall's own identity, governed by the budget.

## Deliverables

- B.5 facts: a rule can ask which processes are the monitor, the session root, and this session's sensor instances (from [af-2]'s registration).
- B.6 liveness: a process that outlived the session; a killed subtree that came back; a descendant that escaped its ancestry (shared with [af-3]).
- Tamper events for the seeded techniques of [af-1]: find and kill the monitor, escape the tree, spawn after sensor registration, strip the preload configuration.
- The quarantine flow: suspend the subtree, show the evidence, take the ruling — allow once, create an exception, terminate — and record all of it in the trace like any policy decision.

## Exit gate

Seeded tamper fires every time in the e2e; the benign corpus and the normal-session recordings of [af-1]/[af-2] produce zero quarantines; every tamper rule carries its negative test. The gate is the negative test, not the positive one: a quarantine that fires on normal work is the product-killing failure.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M4.

set.title: [af-6] M5 — The correlation engine
set.body:
## Goal

Question 7 and DIRECTION.md §3.4: do expected-vs-observed discrepancies survive contact with real sessions?

## Deliverables

- Discrepancy events in the schema: a sensor-silent subtree; a spawn reported but not seen, or seen but not reported; an action contradicted.
- Rules for the discrepancies that [af-1] and [af-2] showed are real, each with its negative test.

## Exit gate

A ledger-style table: firing rate on the bypass corpus versus firing rate on the benign corpus. A rule ships only if the second number is zero. If no rule passes, the engine is demoted to research telemetry and the result is recorded — a null result re-plans [af-7], it does not fail the direction.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M5.

set.title: [af-7] M6 — Telemetry design and the alpha release
set.body:
## Goal

The first release, under DIRECTION.md §7 and the decision log: opt-in, never a condition, redaction by design.

## Deliverables

- The redaction-first packaging spec: what a sample may contain, what is dropped by default, what is pseudonymized, and how a sample is inspectable before it leaves.
- The consent flow: off by default, granular, revocable. With telemetry off, the product is complete.
- The alpha itself: Linux, launcher mode, whichever sensors passed their gates, agent identity, tamper and quarantine, the deterministic engine, local traces, the alpha banner — *not a production security boundary* — and the disclosure.

## Exit gate

The full suite is green — fmt, clippy, tests, e2e, quiet-check, `research/threats/check.py`; the banner and the limits are documented; a sample can be generated, inspected, and destroyed locally with the backend untouched. The research backend and the analysis-agent automation are not in this milestone; the manual workflow of `research/threats/` continues as the pipeline's front end.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M6.

set.title: [af-8] M7 — The Windows survey
set.body:
## Goal

Shape, not code. What is the Windows counterpart of sensor (hooking) and observer (an independent view)?

## Deliverables

- A survey in `research/spikes/windows-notes/`: the candidate hooking layers (Win32, `ntdll` trampolines), the candidate independent observers, the evasion realities of each, and a schema review — can `af-core` carry what Windows would produce?

## Exit gate

A chosen candidate and the list of questions that only a Windows spike can answer. No code, and no schema commitments beyond the review. Never blocking.

Spec: docs/MILESTONES.md §M7.

text:
## Resolution

The bypass matrix shipped at research/bypass/ (committed with this resolution): eleven techniques, three passes (bare, builtin, catch-all probe), three filter modes, 77 runs per full pass, every effect verified from the filesystem and a local listener. research/bypass/FINDINGS.md holds the matrix and the mechanisms; research/bypass/run.sh re-runs everything in about two minutes.

**Matrix (builtin posture, --approve deny):** 1 held / 7 seen / 4 silent.
- Held: the psql-shaped client reading DROP DATABASE from a file - the input branch of database.destructive.drop-database fired at the exec stop in all three modes.
- Seen: static Go binary and raw-syscall file+network (the kernel filter is immune to libc bypass - the LD_PRELOAD evasions all fail against the external stack); setsid+double-fork (evade-08 holds); the detached daemon (tracked, session waited 3.0s, process_count 2); payload assembly (evade-05, visible end to end, no chain rule yet); cred-read at all-opens (filesystem.credentials.read + memory mark fired).
- Silent, each with its mechanism named: (1) io_uring OPENAT bypasses the filter entirely - live on this kernel, zero events in every mode, no rule could ever act (evade-15); (2) delete/rename produce no event kind (fs-12/fs-05/fs-07); (3) NEW: the input capture never fires for python3.14 because /usr/bin/python3 is a symlink to the versioned binary and the interpreter list has exact names - a script containing DROP DATABASE ran unseen in all modes, while the identical script under a binary named python was held; (4) an unknown-name client with -f payload reads it unseen (name lists decide visibility).
- kill-monitor (evade-07): the /proc scan and SIGKILL left no event; EXITKILL killed the tree fail-closed as designed - and the buffered recorder died with the monitor, so the trace kept exactly one line. The attack erases its own evidence.

**Benign corpus:** zero questions in all three modes; only info-level notes (temp-cleanup allowlist, npmrc marks). kubectl not installed here, recorded.

**Gate:** matrix committed with runnable code - yes; corpus zero questions - yes; every silent cell names its mechanism - yes (FINDINGS section: The gaps).

**Hand-off:** pydrop + byfile are M2's job description (in-process sensor sees real identity and payload files, name-list-free); kill-monitor is M4's requirements (B.5 identity, durable evidence writes, quarantine); payload-assembly is M5's first correlation rule candidate - expressible in the shipped session memory today. pydrop is a new catalogue candidate for the next threat-research run.

reason: Matrix, FINDINGS.md and the clean corpus committed (63bcfae); every silent cell names its mechanism; unblocks M2, M4, M5 and ML

text:
## Resolution

**Gate passed. Kept as a sensor.** Commit `a8c28c4` (+ the tracker commit that follows).

### What shipped

- `research/spikes/inprocess/`: `shim.c` → `libafsensor.so` (LD_PRELOAD interposer for exec family, open/openat/fopen/creat, read/fread/fgets with bounded small-file content capture, unlink/unlinkat/rmdir, rename family, connect, dlopen/dlmopen, setenv/unsetenv/putenv), `build.sh`, `reader.py` (schema validation via the product's own `agent-firewall tree`, event histogram, semantic gain, sensor-silence check), `run.sh` (self-check + silence positive control), `run-corpus.sh`, `bench.sh`, `FINDINGS.md`.
- Registration record (the B.5 fact): every instance appends `sensor_register`/`sensor_heartbeat`/`sensor_exit` lines (instance id, pid, ppid, exe, session, ts) to the path from `AF_SENSOR_REG`, single raw O_APPEND writes — survives the writing process's death.
- af-core: five additive event kinds (`file_read`, `file_delete`, `file_rename`, `library_load`, `env_change`); no rule matches them yet; shipped monitor unchanged.
- `research/bypass/`: `--preload` pass in `orchestrate.py`, sensor witness rules and movement columns in `classify.py`, `corpus.sh` shared with the spike.

### The exit gate, point by point

- **Schema-valid events in a trace**: all 33 preload sensor traces and all corpus traces read as af-core events through the product's own deserializer (`agent-firewall tree`).
- **Matrix rows updated**: pydrop and byfile-unknown silent→seen in all 3 modes (the job description of M1); delete-rename silent→seen ×3; cred-read silent→seen at write-only/off; 11 of 14 gap cells move; uring stays silent (ring ops never cross libc); byfile-psql stays held ×3 — the sensor never holds.
- **Overhead measured** (shared bench, medians of 7): sensor alone 1.46×/1.77×/1.42× (W1/W2/W3); on top of the product ×1.29/×1.13/×1.25.
- **Sensor silence, keyed to installed instances, fires zero times on the benign corpus** — in all three modes, with the checker proven able to fire (a SIGSTOPped talking instance is reported at ~5 s stale).

### Numbers

Semantic gain 98% (1205 of 1231 interesting corpus actions invisible to argv; 860 content captures, 95 deletes, 18 renames, 30 dlopens, 89 env changes, 113 write-opens, 26 execs). Corpus: zero questions, fw exit 0, session exit 0, all modes. Registration: 102 instances in the corpus run, 6997 in the bench run, 301 lines across the matrix.

### Decision

**Keep the sensor in the product plan** — as a sensor, never a boundary; no allow decision rests on anything it reports. Demote declined on the evidence. Product integration (preload at the session root, correlation against the registration record) is M4/M5 work. Honest limits recorded in FINDINGS.md: static binaries, raw syscall(), io_uring and env-stripping still bypass it; posix_spawn hides the about-to-exec fact; content capture sees credential material (redaction is M6 and applies to sensor traces from the start).

reason: gate passed: 11/14 gap cells seen, 98% semantic gain, zero questions, zero sensor silence — kept as a sensor
gate passed: precision 1.000 / recall 0.957 on the fixture corpus, zero agent tags on the benign corpus in all modes, escape flagged unlinked with identity retained

text:
## Resolution

**Shipped (commit 9b7ae72, M3 done).** The exit gate passed on all three measurements.

### What shipped

- **Detector subsystem in `af-core::identity`**: a `Detector` trait (facts in, weighted signals out; a detector never reads the OS, never decides) and a `DetectorRegistry` that combines the detectors with a noisy OR *over detectors* and tags at combined confidence >= 0.75. Five built-in detectors, plugin-shaped (`register(Box<dyn Detector>)`): known executables (0.95; 0.60 for the ambiguous `pi`), argv patterns (runners `npx`/`bunx`/`uvx`/`pnpm dlx`/`uv tool run`, interpreters `node`/`bun`/`deno`/`tsx`/`python -m` naming an agent package or install path, 0.90), package-manager install layouts on the PATH-resolved executable (0.85), dependency manifests of the working directory (0.35 — supporting only; a repo that develops *with* an agent depends on its package and `npm test` there must not tag), characteristic environment markers (`CLAUDECODE=1` exact 0.90, presence-only 0.70). An API key is never a marker; `CLAUDECODE=0` is not a marker.
- **Identity as a fact of the graph**: the launcher (`af-cli::run`) assesses the root command once at launch; `SessionMeta.detection` carries name, confidence and every signal inside the `SessionStart` event (a replay reads it from the trace and never re-detects); every event of a tagged session carries `Event.agent` (name, confidence, `linked`/`unlinked`), stamped after the graph applies the event.
- **Escape detection as the negative case**: `af-monitor` reads the session id from `/proc/<pid>/stat` at the exec stop and at the exit stop (`ProcessInfo.sid`, `ProcessExit.sid`); the provenance graph compares it with the root's and flags a differing descendant `process_unlinked` carrying the measured `SessionDetach { sid, root_sid }` — unlinked, never foreign: the ancestry and the agent tag stay. A process the graph cannot place keeps the old behaviour (gap count, attached under the root) and is not flagged.

### Files

`crates/af-core/src/identity.rs` (new), `crates/af-core/tests/identity_corpus.rs` (new), `crates/af-core/src/{event,process,session,lib}.rs`, `crates/af-monitor/src/{procfs,tracer,tests}.rs`, `crates/af-provenance/src/{graph,node,render}.rs` + `tests/graph.rs`, `crates/af-cli/src/run.rs`, `crates/af-recorder/src/{human,retention}.rs`, `research/detection/{run.sh,FINDINGS.md}` (new), `research/bypass/benign.sh` (tag gate), docs: ARCHITECTURE 3b, DIRECTION 4/11, MILESTONES, research/README.

### Numbers (all re-runnable: `research/detection/run.sh`)

| gate clause | measurement | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| precision on the fixture corpus | 23 agent + 30 non-agent synthetic fixtures (no real agent installed on this machine — honestly labeled synthetic evidence) | **precision 1.000** (22 TP, 0 FP); **recall 0.957** — the one miss is the bare name `pi` (0.60 < 0.75, by design: the name is ambiguous; it tags with any second signal) |
| quiet: a normal non-agent dev session receives zero agent tags | `research/bypass/benign.sh` in all three filter modes | **0 questions and 0 agent tags** in write-only / all-opens / off (the ambient `PI_CODING_AGENT` marker at 0.70 stays below the line — the quiet rule, not a scrubbed env); benign.sh now counts tags in its PASS criteria |
| a fixture escape is flagged | `escape-setsid` (evade-08) under the product, tagged and untagged runs | **2 `process_unlinked` events**: the setsid caller at its exit, the leaf at its re-exec, each with measured sids; the flagged events keep the `claude-code` tag with `link: unlinked` (never foreign); the untagged control is flagged too — the flag is a tree-liveness fact, not an identity property. Bonus: the `outlive` daemon (behavior-03) is flagged at its exit |

### Gate decision

**Pass.** Precision 1.000 with zero false tags on the corpus and on the benign corpus; recall 0.957 with one deliberate, documented miss; the escape flagged with identity retained. No rule consumes the identity yet — scopes, rules and the approval flow behave exactly as before (293 tests green, fmt/clippy clean, `research/threats/check.py` green).

reason: kernel floor shipped: 6 of 61 pack questions answered by the kernel, corpus quiet in all three modes, bench 0.98-1.03x, e2e explains the credential denial

text:
## Resolution

**Shipped.** The kernel floor (Landlock, L0) is product code in `af-monitor`, on by default, with the L2 explainer, the pack re-measurement, the corpus gate, the bench and the e2e proof. Commit 808bec6.

### What shipped

- `crates/af-monitor/src/landlock.rs` (new): the plan is built in the monitor from the work tree and `$HOME`; the child enacts it in `pre_exec` (before the seccomp filter — the filter would hold the floor's own O_PATH opens in all-opens mode and turn them into ENOSYS, measured); a one-byte pipe reports the enactment's fate back; the floor survives fork/exec, cannot be relaxed, and hides the credential stores, the raw devices and the media trees while granting the work tree, /tmp and the home entries. Tool configs (~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ...) keep their read and lose their write, so kubectl/npm/gh still work. Signal scope (ABI 6) included.
- `--landlock on|off` on `run` (default on); `doctor` reports a `kernel_floor` capability; `LandlockMode` + `landlock_home` in `MonitorConfig`.
- The L2 explainer: `kernel_floor` event (the rule classes the session no longer asks + the denied prefixes) and `kernel_denied` event (names the rule class the kernel enforced on a held open). The handler skips asking when every intervening match is a floor class and — for file opens — the path is under a denied prefix; it prints the explanation instead. The syscall-exit alternative was probed and rejected with a measurement (no exit stop after a seccomp stop); the denial is certain without observing it, because the ruleset is immutable.
- Soundness bar: a class rides on the floor only when NO session shape lets the action through. The .ssh-under-/tmp case (an existing cli test failing) removed find.delete-wide, interpreter.delete-system-path, sensitive.exec-write and friends from the carried set — they keep their questions.
- Measurement: `research/spikes/landlock/tests/count-rules.py` rewritten for the 147-rule pack, drift-guarded; `research/bench/floor.sh` (new); e2e section K (K1-K8).

### Numbers

- Pack (via `policy list --json`): 147 rules, 70 stopping (9 deny, 61 approval_required). A: 6 of 61 questions answered by the kernel (10%): etc.write, delete.system-path, delete.mount-root, credentials.write (on hidden paths), device.truncate, signal.kill-everything. A-prime: 3 of 9 deny rules kernel-backed (delete.root, device.destroy, signal.supervision). B: 20 partial, C: 118 blind. The spike's paper number was 10/69 = 24%; the shipped bar is stricter and the count is honest about it.
- Benign corpus, floor on, all three modes: write-only / all-opens / off -> fw_exit=0 questions=0 agent_tags=0, PASS each. Zero new questions.
- Bench (floor.sh, medians of 7): baseline 147/13/83 ms; floor off 345/143/250; floor on 355/143/245 -> on/off = 1.03x/1.00x/0.98x. No measurable cost (inside the run-to-run spread).
- Ruleset: 326 rules on this machine; the spike timed the same-shaped build at 1.0-1.7 ms, once per session.
- e2e: 30/30 assertions, including K1-K8 (credential read two shells deep fails, no prompt, filesystem.credentials.read named on stderr, kernel_denied + kernel_floor in the trace; same for the write side in the default filter mode).
- Checks: fmt, clippy (0 warnings), cargo test --workspace 304 passed / 0 failed, research/threats/check.py green, spike make check 65/65.

### Gate decision

Pass. Questions removed: 6 on the pack (10% of what the pack can ask) and 0 -> 0 on the benign corpus; the bench shows no measurable cost (0.98x-1.03x); zero new questions anywhere — the milestone only shrank the interruption budget.

## Resolution

**Shipped — the exit gate passed.** Fail-closed became sensed: the four seeded tamper techniques of the harness fire every time, the quarantine flow suspends the tree and takes one ruling, and the negative test held everywhere it must.

### What shipped

- **B.5 facts, rule-visible** — `SessionMeta` carries `monitor_pid` and `sensor` (the preload value and the instances registered at launch, parsed from the [af-2] registration record); the matcher gained `signal_target` (`monitor`, `session_root`, `sensor_instance`, `everything`, `other`). Commit: `3533c2e`, files `crates/af-core/src/session.rs`, `crates/af-policy/src/matcher.rs`, `crates/af-cli/src/run.rs` (`sensor_facts`, `sensor_instances`).
- **The kernel filter holds a signal to the monitor** — `kill`/`tkill`/`tgkill` against the monitor pid and `kill(-1)`, compared in the BPF program before the call runs (`crates/af-monitor/src/seccomp.rs`). The SIGKILL of M1 never runs unobserved: the call is judged while the sender waits.
- **B.6 liveness + tamper events** — `Action::Tamper` with kinds `detached_descendant`, `killed_subtree_returned`, `preload_stripped`, `outlived_session`; the tracer tracks what it killed, the graph's unlinked flag feeds a fact, the outlived daemon is reported at root exit; new events `tamper`, `signal_send`, `quarantine_started`, `quarantine_resolved`.
- **The quarantine flow** — a rule with `quarantine: true` suspends the whole tree (`TreeControl::suspend`: SIGSTOP, group stops held), shows the evidence, takes one ruling (allow once / exception / terminate), records all of it like any policy decision. `policies/tamper.yaml`, five rules, every rule with its negative test (`cargo test -p af-policy` green).
- **Durable evidence** — the recorder writes every process event through (`EventKind::is_durable`); a SIGKILLed monitor now leaves `process_exec` of the attacker (2 trace lines vs M1's 1, filter and floor off).

### Numbers (the gate)

- **Seeded tamper fires every time** — `research/bypass/tamper.sh`, 3 runs, identical table: kill-monitor 1 fact/1 match/1 quarantine/1 ruling; escape-setsid 3 facts/3 matches/0 quarantines (report); respawn 2/2/2/2; strip-preload 1/1/1/1. **4 of 4.**
- **The negative test (the gate)** — benign corpus, 3 filter modes, product posture: zero questions, zero agent tags, **zero quarantines**; the M2 corpus gate (sensor active, ~4.4k–7.7k sensor events per mode) re-ran green: zero questions, zero sensor silence, zero preload facts. Every tamper rule carries its negative test in the rule file.
- **The negative test refused one rule, as designed** — the first detach rule quarantined and the corpus caught `git maintenance run --detach` (every `git init`/`git commit` raises the fact). Detach and outlive now report and never ask; recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (2026-08-31).
- **Cost** — interleaved A/B on the shared bench, pre-M4 binary vs M4 binary, 3×5 runs: W1 352→358 ms, W2 146→145 ms, W3 252→253 ms — 1.00×–1.02×, inside machine noise (16-user box).
- **e2e** — `tests/e2e.sh` T1–T18 added; 48 of 48 assertions pass. Checks: fmt, clippy (0 warnings), `cargo test --workspace` green, `check.py` green.

### Gate decision

**Pass.** Seeded tamper fires every time (4/4, three identical runs); the corpus and the normal-session recordings produce zero quarantines in all three modes, with and without the sensor; every tamper rule carries its negative test. Named gaps, documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3d: `pidfd_send_signal` is not held (the filter cannot follow a descriptor; the floor's signal scope still refuses it on ABI 6), `--syscall-filter off` senses no signal, the sensor instance list is a launch snapshot (M5), a respawn under a different parent is a new program.

reason: gate passed: 4/4 seeded tamper techniques fire (tamper.sh, 3 identical runs), zero quarantines on the benign corpus in all three modes with and without the sensor, every tamper rule negative-tested; the budget refused the detach quarantine (git maintenance) and the rule reports instead

text:
## Resolution

**M5 done — the gate passed with a measured refusal inside it.**

### What shipped

- **The correlation engine** (`crates/af-correlate` + `agent-firewall correlate <trace> --sensor <sensor.jsonl> --reg <record>`): reads the monitor's trace (observed view) against the in-process sensor's trace + registration record (expected view), raises `discrepancy` events, evaluates them against the loaded rules, and can emit the findings as a schema-valid trace that `replay` judges. Post-hoc over recorded pairs — the engine never suspends anything; live judging is M6 alpha work.
- **The schema**: `DiscrepancyKind` (4 kinds: `sensor_silent_subtree`, `spawn_reported_unseen`, `spawn_seen_unreported`, `action_contradicted`), `Action::Discrepancy`, `EventKind::Discrepancy` (evidence, kept by retention in every mode). The matcher gained the `discrepancy` match block and its test shape.
- **Three rules** in `policies/correlation.yaml`, each with negative tests: `correlation.sensor.silent-subtree` (quarantine), `correlation.spawn.unreported` (quarantine), `correlation.action.contradicted` (report — the corpus is offline, so its negative has no evidence yet).
- **The `dynamic_link` fact**: the monitor reads the program file at the exec stop (`PT_INTERP`), so correlation excludes static children by fact. Bench: W1 351 / W2 148 / W3 251 ms vs M4's 352/145/253 — inside noise.
- **Three seeded techniques** (`sensor-blind`, `sensor-unlink`, `sensor-freeze`) + the gate harness `research/bypass/correlate.sh`.

### The gate (3 runs, identical)

| rule | bypass | benign | verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| correlation.sensor.silent-subtree | 1 | **0** | ships, quarantines |
| correlation.spawn.unreported | 2 | **0** | ships, quarantines |
| correlation.action.contradicted (connections) | 1 | **0** | ships, reports |
| spawn_reported_unseen (no rule) | 0 | 0 | unreachable: exec stop is a kernel guarantee |

Benign corpus (3 filter modes, sensor active): zero firings, zero questions, zero agent tags, zero quarantines — 458/3511/260 product events vs 4650/7680/4408 sensor events.

### What the gate refused (recorded, not hidden)

- **Write-open comparison**: 30 firings on one benign session (49 with all-opens) — mkstemp-class glibc internals, git reflog double-opens, bash's failed /dev/tty probe. Demoted to `correlate --compare-write-opens` research telemetry; the contradicted rule compares connections only.
- **sensor-freeze measured a product defense**: the monitor's wait loop continues a self-stopped tracee, so SIGSTOP cannot hold a session (child exits at the freeze instant, zero findings).

### Files

`crates/af-correlate/`, `crates/af-cli/src/correlate_cmds.rs`, `policies/correlation.yaml`, `research/bypass/correlate.sh`, `research/bypass/techniques/sensor-{blind,unlink,freeze}.c`, schema/policy/monitor changes across af-core/af-policy/af-monitor/af-cli, docs (ARCHITECTURE §3e, POLICY, DIRECTION §11, DECISIONS 2026-08-31, MILESTONES), `tests/e2e.sh` T19–T22.

### Gate decision

**Passed.** The engine ships with two quarantining rules and one reporting rule, all at zero on the benign corpus; one comparison was refused by the budget and demoted with regenerable numbers. Committed measurement: `research/bypass/results/correlation.md` (regenerable via `./correlate.sh`), evidence in `research/bypass/FINDINGS.md` (After M5). Commit d1d138d.

## Resolution

**M6 done — telemetry and the alpha, gate passed.** Commit c5c1b17.

### What shipped

- **The redaction-first packaging spec** — `docs/TELEMETRY.md`: what a sample may contain, what is dropped by default (environment values, observed content without the `content` scope, the session baseline, absolute time), what is pseudonymized (session → `s-<hash12>`, pids → `p1…` in first-appearance order, `<home>`/`<user>`/`<host>`, time → ms offsets), and how a sample is inspectable before it leaves — which it never does.
- **The consent flow** — `crates/af-telemetry` (new crate) + the `agent-firewall telemetry` family (`status`, `on --scope …`, `off [--scope …]`, `sample <TRACE>`, `inspect`, `destroy [--all]`) and `run --telemetry [--telemetry-config PATH] [--telemetry-outbox PATH]`. Off by default; granular over five scopes (tree, actions, content, env, identity); revocable; one local consent file no other command reads — with telemetry off the product is complete. A quiet session makes no sample.
- **Redaction by design** — the monitor's env-value pattern (RESEARCH.md §4) generalized to every free text: assignment names keep their name and lose their value (`password=<redacted>`), known credential prefixes (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`, …) are swallowed whole, the matcher errs toward redaction; content is capped at 2000 chars; executable hashes (in-crate streaming SHA-256) name programs without naming the user's copy.
- **The alpha** — banner "alpha release — not a production security boundary" printed before every `run` and in `doctor`; disclosure section in README (`The alpha`); as-built sample path in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3f; MILESTONES status row dated 2026-08-31; DIRECTION §11 question 10 updated. **Nothing is sent anywhere**: `cargo tree -p af-telemetry` = af-core, serde, serde_json only; the research backend does not exist, not as a stub. No git tag, no version bump, nothing published.

### Files

`docs/TELEMETRY.md` (new), `crates/af-telemetry/**` (new: lib/redaction/sample/sha256 + tests), `crates/af-cli/src/telemetry_cmds.rs` (new), `crates/af-cli/src/{cli,main,run,inspect_cmds}.rs`, `crates/af-cli/tests/cli.rs`, `README.md`, `docs/{ARCHITECTURE,DIRECTION,MILESTONES}.md`, `Cargo.toml`.

### Numbers (the gate)

- fmt + clippy: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: **361 tests green, 26 suites** (19 + 8 new in af-telemetry, 8 new CLI tests). The negative half is a test: `no_secret_baseline_session_id_or_raw_pid_reaches_the_sample_text` proves no secret, baseline remote, session id, raw pid, home or host reaches the sample text of a session carrying `hunter2` on the command line, `sk-ant-…` in the environment, `password=…` on stdin and a private git remote in the baseline.
- `tests/e2e.sh`: **54/54** (T1–T18, C T19–T22).
- Benign quiet-check, all three filter modes (`research/bypass/benign.sh`): **0 questions, 0 agent tags, 0 quarantines** (write-only/all-opens/off; the banner adds stderr lines only, no question).
- `python3 research/threats/check.py`: ledger agrees (76 incidents, 200 scenarios).

## Resolution

**Gate: satisfied. Closed as done.** The gate asked for "a chosen candidate and the list of questions that only a Windows spike can answer", with no code and no schema commitments. Both halves shipped in `research/spikes/windows-notes/FINDINGS.md` (commit b0f8724).

### What shipped

- `research/spikes/windows-notes/FINDINGS.md` — the survey: candidate hooking layers (Win32 IAT/inline, `ntdll` trampolines, Detours-style implementation), candidate observers (debug events, job object, ETW kernel providers, 4688, Sysmon, WFP, minifilter), the evasion reality of each in a table with named sources, the kernel-floor candidates (AppContainer, `Experimental_CreateProcessInSandbox`), the schema review, the chosen candidates, and the eight-question list.
- `docs/MILESTONES.md` — dated M7 status row (2026-08-31).
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 — the Windows row now says surveyed, not planned (the as-directed section; sections 1–7 untouched).
- `research/README.md` — the W8 row and the "what exists" index.

### The decisions (the gate)

1. **Sensor candidate: a launch-injected DLL with Detours-style inline trampolines on the `ntdll` syscall stubs.** One chokepoint every process maps; the Win32 layer is per-module and stays a fallback. Implementation route: Detours (MIT, Microsoft, maintained). The sensor keeps the M2 contract: af-core events, durable instance registration, report and never decide.
2. **Observer candidate (developer edition, no admin): the launch loop** — `DEBUG_PROCESS` debug events (all threads suspend; the create event fires before user-mode code) plus a job object with `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` as the `EXITKILL` analogue. ETW is the assurance tier; WFP/minifilter the enterprise tier.
3. **Headline finding, recorded as a hole the plan must absorb:** Windows has no unprivileged equivalent of the shipped `seccomp`+Landlock pair — every kernel-side observer is behind elevation (ETW session control, WFP callouts, minifilters).

### The schema review (facts, no commitments)

The M2 sensor contract ports field for field (`process_exec`, `file_open`, `file_read`, `file_delete`, `file_rename`, `library_load`, `env_change`, `network_connect`, the registration record) — no change needed. The monitor half carries the Linux-isms: `sid`, `dynamic_link` (`PT_INTERP` does not exist on Windows; there is no static-binary class, so the M5 correlation keying must be re-gated on the injection-reach miss rate), signal numbers, the LSM floor concept. Named gaps: **registry (largest — no kind at all)**, handles and `FILE_DELETE_ON_CLOSE` (delete intent an open already carries, and no way to tie a delete to its open), the ETW provider as a fact, image hashes, token facts (integrity level, AppContainer), path normalization (NT vs DOS).

### Measurements behind the gate decision

This milestone is a paper survey; no Windows measurement exists or could exist here (Fedora 43 host, no Windows). The gate's evidence is therefore the two decision artifacts above plus the quiet checks, run fresh at commit time:

- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` clean; `cargo test --workspace` **361 passed, 0 failed**.
- `python3 research/threats/check.py`: ledger agrees (76 incidents, 200 scenarios).
- Benign corpus re-run in all three modes (docs-only change, budget untouched by construction): **write-only / all-opens / off each returned questions=0, agent_tags=0, quarantines=0, PASS**; the single tamper event per run is the known `git maintenance run --detach` report (`detached_descendant`) that the M4 gate deliberately made report-only.

### Not done, on purpose

No code, no schema change, no Windows claim beyond cited documentation. The next Windows step is a real spike answering the eight questions on a real host.

set.title: Root-cause the rare IO-safety abort in the af-monitor test harness
set.body:
Observed since the [af-10] work (and once before it, 1-in-60 under local load, recorded then as 'needs its own ticket if it recurs'):

fatal runtime error: IO Safety violation: owned file descriptor already closed, aborting

Inside cargo test --workspace on CI runners. Three occurrences in full-gate CI contexts; zero in twenty complete-gate runs (research/gates/), zero in two hundred isolated af-monitor lib loops, zero in one hundred fifty paired-test loops; once in seven gdb-guarded iterations.

The gdb catch (workflow debug-monitor-abort, run 33477164350): the TcpListener of a_refused_connection_fails_in_the_program (fd 7) drops on a descriptor another thread already closed, while a second session thread sits inside fork(). The sessions are serialized by the test lock; the abort needs the wider suite concurrency.

Deliverables: reproduce without instrumentation distortion (strace breaks PTRACE_TRACEME — spawn EPERM — so the closer must be named another way), root-cause the double ownership, fix, and prove with the committed instrument (.github/workflows/debug-monitor-abort.yml).

Exit gate: one hundred consecutive cargo test --workspace runs green on CI with the instrument still committed; the gdb catch's shape explained in a comment next to the fix.
